artDirection.styleSuffix: late-16-bit arcade side-scroller pixel art, late-SNES / CPS-style polish with subtle early-3D-era material weight, flat orthographic side-view, hard contrast, cinematic dry corporate-apocalypse tone, clean rigid silhouette, isolated on a pure magenta #FF00FF background, exact flat key-color background with no near-magenta noise or stray key-colored squares, high readability at the requested canvas size, disciplined color palette (<=48 colors), no anti-aliased blur, no soft gradients, sharp pixel-perfect edges, dithered shading and crisp indexed-color highlights only, black 1px outline where silhouette meets background, no text or letters unless specified
artDirection.negativePrompt: photorealistic, full 3d render, smooth shaded model, anti-aliasing, blurred edges, painterly, watercolor, soft gradients, lens flare, bokeh, depth-of-field, camera grain, motion blur, cel shading, noise, jpeg artifacts, checkerboard background, random colored squares, near-magenta background artifacts, key-color pixels inside the artwork, text labels, watermark, signature, logo, extra limbs, melted anatomy
artDirection.silhouetteRule: Every character / weapon / moving entity must be isolated on the pure magenta background so an alpha key recovers a clean transparent PNG. Background pixels must be exactly #FF00FF only, with no checkerboard, no random squares, no near-magenta off-color pixels, and no background elements inside the keyed rectangle. Do not use #FF00FF or near-#FF00FF colors in the artwork, shading, highlights, shadows, or dithering.
artDirection.downscale: Generate at exactly 1x, 2x, or 3x the final output dimensions, then downsample to output dimensions using nearest-neighbor. Never bilinear or lanczos for pixel art.

scaleContract.stagePrompt: Runtime scale reference: the arena is 1280x720. Fighters render unscaled from 64x64 sprite cells, with the readable body and sim hitbox about 28x56 pixels. Stage props, platforms, doors, monitors, furniture, racks, rails, wall panels, podiums, crowd elements, and debris must be proportioned so a 56px-tall fighter reads human-sized in the scene. Avoid giant foreground props that make fighters look miniature and avoid tiny background details that make fighters look oversized.

stageDepth.previewThumb: Preview thumbnail shows the whole playable arena composition. It may include all depth layers, but should still make the 56px fighter scale feel plausible.
stageDepth.sky: Deepest layer. Treat it as distant atmosphere or architecture behind the play plane. No gameplay-scale foreground props, no walkable-looking surfaces, no large objects that appear close to the fighters.
stageDepth.farParallax: Far background layer, slower than gameplay space. Objects should read distant, lower contrast, and smaller/detail-reduced than the fighters. Use architecture, racks, crowd lights, or long room cues, not foreground furniture.
stageDepth.midParallax: Middle background layer behind platforms and fighters. Props can be recognizable, but they must sit behind the combat plane and should not look like interactable platforms.
stageDepth.nearParallax: Nearest backdrop dressing layer, drawn behind platforms and fighters. Keep readable foreground silhouettes mostly around edges or lower bands, but do not create walkable ledges or giant close-up props.
stageDepth.platform: Gameplay surface texture. This is the actual walkable plane. Tile detail must be sized for 28x56 fighters standing on it; avoid perspective props or whole objects that imply the surface is far away.
stageDepth.platformEdge: Thin gameplay ledge rim. It must read as the top edge of a walkable platform at fighter scale, not a distant trim or oversized wall.
stageDepth.wall: Solid floor/body fill and left/right arena boundary texture. It is close to the gameplay plane but not a character-scale prop layer; avoid doors, furniture, or objects that imply incorrect scale.

postProcess: 3. Key near-#FF00FF background to alpha (RGB-distance tolerance 24).
5. Index to <=32 colors (optional; preserves palette discipline).

gemini.instructionStyle: Use the prompt verbatim. Preserve exact layout, grid, dimensions, magenta key background, and post-process requirements.

gpt.instructionStyle: Use the prompt verbatim. Preserve exact layout, grid, dimensions, magenta key background, and post-process requirements.

_sharedRules.layoutDirective: Final runtime sprite sheet grid: EXACTLY 6 columns x 12 rows, each frame centered in its 192x192 generation cell (target 64x64 after 3x nearest-neighbor downscale), no gutters. Prompt generation uses packed 8 columns x 2 rows sheets; local tooling assembles populated packed cells into the final 6x12 runtime sheet. Character facing camera-right in every populated frame. Every populated character must stay fully inside its own cell; no head, hair, arms, legs, cloth, or motion pose may cross a vertical or horizontal cell cut. Blank cells must be pure #FF00FF only. Character silhouette is a TALL HUMAN FIGURE with aspect approximately 1:2 — roughly 28 pixels wide by 56 pixels tall in the 64x64 final cell. Do NOT draw a square silhouette. Center the body horizontally with about 18 pixels of pure magenta #FF00FF padding on each side, and about 4 pixels of magenta padding above the head and below the feet. The figure's in-sim hitbox is 28 wide by 56 tall; the drawn silhouette should read as roughly that shape at a glance so combat reads correctly. Weapons NOT drawn on this sheet (weapons are a separate layer).

taunt.sama: index finger raised as if consulting a graph only they can see
taunt.darrius: slow legalistic empty-hand gesture as if closing an invisible folder; do not draw the folder
taunt.demis: drawing a small diagram in the air

generationStrategy: Strategy A (preferred): generate three packed prompt sheets per character. Each prompt is 1536x384 with an 8x2 grid of exact 192x192 cells, no gutters, cells 1-15 populated, and the bottom-right cell 16 pure #FF00FF. The runtime uses 41 animation frames; the final pack's four overflow populated cells are ignored by assembly. Downscale each pack exactly 3x to 512x128 nearest-neighbor, then assemble populated runtime cells into the final 384x768 runtime sheet.
Strategy B (fallback): ask for the full 6x12 grid in one shot with strict layoutDirective. Expect lower alignment reliability and more re-rolls.

Right cell (legendary, Heat-Sink Greatsword): oversized finned heat sink slab forged into a greatsword, glowing thermal core, brutal rectangular silhouette.

darrius.base: Character B epic/legendary weapon sheet, 1x2 strip. Left cell (epic, Red-Team Pike): long polearm with forked testing spearhead and red warning tags, clean pike silhouette, mass at the forked tip. Right cell (legendary, Guardrail Greatsword): bent highway guardrail with bolted grip, massive protective slab weapon, bureaucratic safety made violent.

demis.base: Character C epic/legendary weapon sheet, 1x2 strip. Left cell (epic, Go Board Maul): square board slab with inset stone studs mounted as a maul, sober academic brutality, mass at the board end. Right cell (legendary, AlphaFold Blade): rigid spiraling protein structure sharpened into a blade, elegant scientific silhouette, not soft, clearly a sword.

mark.base: Character D epic/legendary weapon sheet, 1x2 strip. Left cell (epic, Shareholder Sauce Club): thick crystallized condiment bottle forged into a cudgel, curved bottle silhouette, ridiculous but physically blunt. Right cell (legendary, Quest Flail): cracked headset swung from an elite strap like a flail, heavy visor mass at the striking end, clean silhouette.

_sharedRules.layoutDirective: Single locked-slot placeholder icon, readable at 48px, isolated on pure magenta #FF00FF.

locked_weapon.base: Locked weapon slot placeholder: dark silhouette of a generic short weapon inside a corporate audit stamp frame, muted greyscale palette, subtle chain-and-padlock overlay across the silhouette, conveys 'reserved, not yet released' without text, severe and bureaucratic tone.
